description: Number of 8-connected components of the final centreline (target) and of the visible centreline (target or u_line) after dilation by half the gap tolerance c, and their ratio to the number of centreline branches, for the 50 images of the multi-illumination aerial set: per image (frames), per viewpoint (by_view: median and range over its 10 images), per outcrop type and over all 50 images.
paper_items: supplement S4: table of the number of connected components of the final centreline
supplement S4, text: 19 centreline branches at the flat-outcrop viewpoint, median of 61 components at a gap tolerance of 0

definitions.dilation: Euclidean disc of radius r = (c/2) / nominal pixel size (pixels): distance transform <= r
definitions.reported: number of components, and number of components / number of centreline branches

notes: At c = 0 the gaps of the visible centreline (target or u_line) are not all places where the trace cannot be seen: the label program removes from target the centreline pixels within 2 px of an unclear (U) line, within 2 px of a transition between visible and occluded parts and inside the other marked areas, and u_line returns only the pixels of the unclear windows themselves, so that a few pixels stay empty between the two layers. From c = 0.10 m (dilation radius of 6 px or more) these gaps are bridged.
Dilation also joins neighbouring traces, so a ratio of components to branches below 1 at a large tolerance does not mean that the traces have no gaps.
The 10 frames of a viewpoint differ only in illumination and render seed: the number of centreline branches is the same, target and u_line change with the brightness check.
At the standalone-outcrop viewpoints the pixel size is not uniform within the frame; the tolerance in metres holds near the target point.
